designs.summaryForFounder: Three money faults are confirmed: two people banking the same receipt at the same moment both succeed; a payment a driver takes at a door with no signal is left out when the trip's cash is counted at day-end; and undoing a doorstep cash payment after day-end takes it out of the van's money a second time instead of the office's. The fix locks each receipt while it is banked, undone or counted, so only one of those can win. Day-end counts every payment of the trip however it arrived, an undo takes the money from wherever it really is, and the driver's phone cannot check the vehicle in until its payments have reached the office. Two decisions are yours: whether a payment that reaches the office after its trip was settled is refused, with the driver told to hand the cash to the cashier (recommended), and whether wrong figures in your own records are corrected by one extra balancing entry each, trip by trip with your say (recommended). This revision was written by Opus standing in for Fable.

founderQuestions.question: A driver's phone was dead all evening; the trip was settled at Day-end on the cash counted; next morning the phone sends a Rs 672 cash receipt for that trip. What should happen?
options: A - Refuse it: the phone and its End of day screen tell the driver to hand Rs 672 to the cashier, and the office records it when the cash changes hands
B - Accept it as van cash: the books say the crew still holds Rs 672 on a closed trip, and no screen hands it over
C - Accept it as office cash at once: the books say the office has the money before anyone handed it over
founderQuestions.why: Nothing is ever posted against a closed trip, and the shop's bill is paid when the money really reaches the office. The new check-in gate makes this case rare, because at the godown the phone has signal and sends everything before the vehicle can be checked in.

founderQuestions.question: If the read-only checks find figures already wrong in your own dos database (a receipt banked twice, trip cash booked as over or short, an undo taken from van cash after settlement), may each be corrected with one extra balancing entry, listed for your sign-off trip by trip?
options: A - Yes: one appended correcting entry per case, never an edit, with your say per trip on whether the crew handed that cash over or still holds it
B - No: rebuild dos from the seed, which loses the receipts recorded there
founderQuestions.why: The books stay append-only and every correction is visible. Only you know, per trip, whether the missing cash was handed over or is still with the crew. dos_qa needs neither option: it is rebuilt from the seed.

designs.summaryForFounder: At the van door the crew's phone shows the price before GST as the sale total, so on a Rs 248 bill they ask the shop for Rs 221.40 and the shop is left owing Rs 26.60, even though the books themselves are right. The fix makes the van-sale screen show the full bill amount with GST and a breakdown under it, keeps the bill number and amount on screen after billing, and makes the money screen count a van-sale bill in what is owed at that shop. One question for you: the extra tax on fizzy drinks is not in the price check yet, so should we build this now and let that separate fix close the last gap, or wait until both are ready?

founderQuestions.question: The extra tax on fizzy drinks (28% GST plus 12% cess) is not in the price check yet; that is a separate, lower-priority fix (DOS-079). Should the van-door fix be built now, or held until both are ready together?
options: A: Build now. Every item that carries only GST (the whole catalogue except aerated drinks) is exact at the door at once. On a fizzy drink the screen is short by the cess until the other fix, but the bill's own amount is shown right after billing, so the crew still asks for the right money.
B: Hold until the cess fix lands too. Every van sale keeps showing the price without GST, and the crew keeps asking for too little, for weeks.
founderQuestions.why: Holding keeps every van sale short by the full GST (5-28%) at the moment money changes hands, to avoid a much smaller cess-only error on one product family. After billing the screen shows the bill itself, which already includes cess. We also recommend moving the cess fix ahead of the rest of its group.

designs.summaryForFounder: When a shop is closed or refuses the goods, the bill rides back on the van, and today the godown can never load it again properly: it drops off the loading list for good and the next van quietly carries it off with no count, no challan and no e-way bill check. Fix: the bill waits on its van until the vehicle is checked in, then comes back on the planning board and the loading list and goes out on a fresh load sheet for its next trip, with the manager's approval, the count, a new challan and the e-way bill check on the whole load. One question for you: may a van still leave with a bill nobody counted out at the godown (recommended: no, the van waits for its load sheet).

founderQuestions.question: May a trip leave the godown with a bill that nobody counted out on a load sheet? Today it can: the bill is marked dispatched quietly at departure and no challan or e-way bill covers it, and every bill that comes back undelivered takes this road on its second trip.
options: A: No. The trip is refused until the godown builds and confirms the load sheet; the driver's screen names the uncounted bills.
B: Yes. Keep the quiet departure but write on the trip that it left without a load sheet so the desk can see it.
founderQuestions.why: Under A nothing leaves without the manager's approval, the blind count, a challan and the e-way bill check, which is the 2026-09-05 decision and DOS-043. A load worth Rs 1 lakh or more can no longer go out without its e-way bill number. B is half a day cheaper and never holds a crew back, but the count, the challan and the e-way bill stay optional on every bill that comes back.

founderQuestions.question: A driver took ₹672 cash at a shop with no signal. The trip was checked in and settled at the office before his phone sent that receipt, for example because he signed out keeping it or checked in from another phone. The receipt arrives the next morning. What should happen?
options: A: Refuse it on the phone. The driver's Needs-attention list says the trip was already settled and asks him to hand the ₹672 to the cashier, who records it at the office. A cheque is handled the same way. A UPI payment is accepted, because that money is already in your account.
B: Accept it as cash the crew still holds on a closed trip. The books then show the crew holding ₹672, with no screen to hand it over.
C: Accept it as cash already in the office. The books then show the money in the till before anyone has handed it over.
founderQuestions.why: Money follows the hand-over. Only A keeps the van, the office till and the shop's bill true at every moment. The new rule that the van cannot be checked in while the phone still holds unsent records makes this case rare.

founderQuestions.question: A bill comes back undelivered and goes out again on a later trip. May that trip leave the godown without a load sheet that counted the bill out?
options: A: No. The trip waits until the godown builds the load sheet, the manager approves it and the count is confirmed. The driver's screen names the bills still to be counted. Every van then leaves with a challan, and with an e-way bill number when the load is big enough to need one.

B: Yes, as today, but the trip and the bill are marked 'left without a load sheet' so the desk can see it. Nothing blocks the crew, but those bills travel with no count, no challan and no e-way bill check.
founderQuestions.why: A matches what you decided for load-out on 2026-09-05 and in DOS-043. With B, every returned bill goes out uncounted, and a van can be stopped on the road for a missing e-way bill.

founderQuestions.question: Checks that change nothing may find money figures already wrong in your own database: a payment banked twice, van cash missed at a settlement, or an undo taken from the van after day-end. How should they be put right?
options: A: Add one correcting entry for each case, never editing the old ones. You see the list and approve it trip by trip, including whether the crew handed that cash over or still has it.
B: Rebuild your database from the demo data. Anything recorded in it since then is lost.
founderQuestions.why: The books can only be corrected by adding entries, and only you know whether a crew handed the cash over. The QA database is rebuilt from the fixed demo data anyway, so it needs neither.
